title: 103 Pharma Firms Face NPPA Demand Notices Over Alleged Medicine Overcharging
summary: New Delhi: The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) has intensified its crackdown on medicine overcharging, issuing 103 demand notices to pharmaceutical manufacturers across the country...

contentHtml:
New Delhi: The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) has intensified its crackdown on medicine overcharging, issuing 103 demand notices to pharmaceutical manufacturers across the country over the last four months for alleged violations of price control norms.

The action, initiated after prima facie cases of overcharging were established, was taken under the provisions of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order (DPCO), 2013, the Government informed the Lok Sabha on Friday.

Raising the issue in the Lok Sabha, MP Shri Robert Bruce C sought details of the penal action initiated by NPPA against distributors for overcharging or artificial retail stock withholding in Tamil Nadu during the last four months. He also sought information on the registration of domestic pharmaceutical manufacturers under the newly launched Form-IA central digital pricing database.

Responding to the query, Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers Anupriya Patel said that the National Pharmaceuticals Pricing Authority (NPPA) is entrusted with implementation of Drugs Price Control Order issued by the DoP, from time to time.

Further he added that NPPA monitors the prices of scheduled as well as non-scheduled medicines under DPCO, 2013 and takes action against manufacturers found overcharging the consumers, based on the references received from various resources including Price Monitoring and Resource Units (PMRUs), State Drugs Controllers, samples purchased from the open market, reports from market data base, complaints reported through the grievance redressal channels.

The suspected cases of overcharging received from above sources are examined and in case a prima facie case of overcharging is made out, action is initiated as per provisions of DPCO, 2013.

The Minister stated that whenever information received from these sources establishes a prima facie case of overcharging, NPPA initiates action in accordance with the provisions of the DPCO, 2013.

She informed the House,

"During the last four months, NPPA has issued 103 demand notices to manufacturers across the country including Tamil Nadu. Further, NPPA does not maintain a state-wise record of overcharging by pharmaceutical companies."

Replying to another part of the question, the Minister clarified that Form-IA, introduced under the Drugs (Prices Control) Amendment Order, 2026, does not require domestic pharmaceutical manufacturers to register their production lines or manufacturing batches. Instead, manufacturers launching an existing new drug formulation whose retail price has already been notified by NPPA during the preceding 12 months are required to adopt the same retail price and intimate NPPA through Form-IA within one month of launch.
